claim: Museo Enzo Ferrari (MEF) sits at Enzo's birth house in central Modena, a few minutes' walk from Modena railway station.
quote: The Enzo Ferrari Museum stands on the very spot where Enzo Ferrari was born and spent his youth: Via Paolo Ferrari 85, in the centre of Modena, just a few minutes' walk from the railway station.

claim: Ferrari sells a combined Museums Pass covering both Maranello and Modena for 38 euro adult / 12 euro under-19 with family, valid 48 hours.
quote: When purchasing the new Ferrari Museums Pass, visitors can access both museums on a single ticket costing 38 euros. Under 19s accompanied by a family member enjoy a special 12 euro rate.

claim: MEF opening hours run 9:30-19:00 April-October (9:00 start June-Aug) and 9:30-18:00 November-March.
quote: April to May: daily 9:30 am to 7 pm; June to August: daily 9:00 am to 7 pm; September to October: daily 9:30 am to 7 pm; November to March: daily 9:30 am to 6 pm.

claim: The Ferrari Factory Panoramic Tour is a 45-minute bus tour around the Fiorano track and factory grounds; visitors stay on board and no photos are allowed.
quote: The 45-minute bus tour takes visitors into the Ferrari factory site and around the Fiorano track and the Company facilities (visitors remain aboard the bus at all times).

claim: Panoramic Tour departs only twice daily (12:30 and 13:30) from the Maranello museum plaza and requires same-day museum ticket plus separate booking code.
quote: The Panoramic Tour shuttle bus departs from the plaza in front of the Ferrari Museum in Maranello, with two bus tour departure times per day (12:30 and 13:30).

claim: Official MEF shuttle from Modena station to Maranello costs about 14.62 euro round-trip with departures 10:45 and 15:15, returns 14:45 and 18:00, stopping at MEF Modena en route.
quote: €14.62 per ticket. Outbound (Modena Station to Ferrari Museum Maranello): 10:45 AM, 3:15 PM. Return: 2:45 PM, 6:00 PM. Both routes include a pit stop at the Enzo Ferrari Museum in Modena.

claim: MUDETEC Lamborghini museum in Sant'Agata Bolognese is open daily 9:30-18:00 (Oct-Apr) and 9:30-19:00 (May-Sep), closed only on August 15 and December 25.
quote: October 1 – April 30: 9:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. (last entry at 5 p.m.); May 2 – September 30: 9:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. (last entry at 6 p.m.)

claim: Lamborghini factory tours from the museum cover the V12 Revuelto line and V10 Huracan line, with small-group time-slot booking mandatory via the Mudetec app.
quote: The V12 line features where the Revuelto's engine and frame come together for the first time and on to the V10 line where the Huracán is born. Tour booking is mandatory, requiring the formation of small groups with admittance at intervals.

claim: The separate Ferruccio Lamborghini Museum at Funo di Argelato (the founder's personal collection, not the factory) is 17 euro adult / 12 euro reduced, closed Mondays.
quote: Standard: €17. Reduced: €12 (students, teachers, seniors 65+, children 6-14). Tuesday to Friday: 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM | 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM. Saturday and Sunday: 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM | 2:00 PM – 6:30 PM. Closed Mondays.

claim: Pagani factory + museum tour at San Cesario costs 60 euro (65 euro from March 1 2026), runs Mon-Fri only, lasts about 1 hour, advance booking mandatory.
quote: The full price is €60.00 (from March 1st 2026 €65.00)... The guided tours are held only with prior booking from Monday to Friday (holidays excluded) and last about 1 hour.

claim: Pagani is the No.1 attraction on TripAdvisor for the area and visitors repeatedly call its hand-built tour superior to Ferrari and Lamborghini factory experiences.
quote: Having had a disappointing 'factory' tour from Ferrari, this one was the real deal... The experience was far superior to the Ferrari and Lamborghini visits on the same day, both in information and pure enjoyment.

claim: Maserati factory tour in Modena is 50 euro adult / 35 euro ages 7-17 for a 75-minute visit; a separate 15 euro showroom tour (40 min) is available; both run Mon-Fri only, closed in August.
quote: Factory Tour (75 minutes): Full price: €50.00... Showroom Tour (40 minutes): Full price: €15.00... Tours operate Monday to Friday on selected dates.

claim: The Stanguellini classic-car museum in central Modena is appointment-only at 15 euro adult / 10 euro child, with hour-long guided tours Mon-Fri 9:30-13:00 and 14:30-18:30.
quote: Visits can be arranged from Monday to Friday from 9:30 to 13:00 and from 14:30 to 18:30 hrs. Full admission is €15 per person, with reduced admission of €10 for children.

claim: Ducati Borgo Panigale museum near Bologna charges 17 euro for museum entry alone and 32 euro for museum + factory tour; factory tours run Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri at 09:30 and 15:30.
quote: The ticket price for the Ducati Museum entrance only is €17, while the ticket with combined entrance to the Ducati Museum and guided factory tour is available at €32. The tour inside the Ducati Factory can be booked every Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday with two rounds of visits, the first at 9:30 and the second at 15:30.

claim: Ducati Museum closes for renovation 14 July - 14 October 2026, but the factory experience still runs during that window.
quote: the museum will be closed to the public from Tuesday, July 14 to Wednesday, October 14 for renovation works. During this period, it will still be possible to take part in the Factory Experience.

claim: Travelers comparing the two Ferrari museums note Modena leans street-car / Enzo biography, Maranello leans F1 / racing, and Modena wins on transport convenience.
quote: In Modena there are more street cars, while in Maranello has more F1/race cars. Modena's museum is much easier to access by public transport, while Maranello is far from the city.

claim: Combining both Ferrari museums plus Lamborghini realistically fills two days; cramming all three plus Pagani into a single day is a frantic rush.
quote: If you're aiming to visit both Ferrari museums and the Lamborghini museum, you're looking at a full two-day itinerary, as trying to cram everything into one day would be a frantic rush.
